title: Glossary.
caption: The terms this paper uses, the names they carry in the code, and, where it differs, the meaning in OpenZeppelin's account or in oz-policy-builder. The vision companion paper has the full glossary.
rows: A bounded set of rules the owner installs so an app can act without a prompt for each call
No single object: one context rule per contract, each with its policies
The JSON the owner submits to install a grant
One target contract, function list, argument conditions and signer threshold, with an optional expiry and cap
At most *limit* charged in the last *P* ledgers, checked at every ledger, so the window slides
`spending_limit` uses the same window boundary. In an oz-policy-builder Intent, `cap` bounds one call (`lte`)
Deriving from a grant a narrower one that allows no call the original does not
A capped rule's charged amounts and their ledgers
A stateless contract that parses and validates a grant document
The pure function that decides an authorization and returns the next spending records; it reads no storage and checks no signature
A contract with `verify(digest, key, signature) -> bool`
The same interface for External signers
A key the account checks through a verifier contract, such as an Ed25519 key or a passkey
Refused on rules the interpreter polices (error {{fact:opb-error-external-signer}})
Another Stellar address that approves through the host, inside the account's own authorization entry (CAP-0071)
Approves in an authorization entry of its own, which binds the rule IDs; the only kind on policed rules
The value that fills a signer: a delegated address, or a verifier contract and key; a document names each signer by its signer ID
One call or contract creation in the request the host passes to `__check_auth`
The same; a context rule matches it
A simulation that runs `__check_auth`, so it predicts a refusal; recording simulation, which discovers which entries a transaction needs, does not
OpenZeppelin's unit of authorization: a context type, signers, policies and an optional `valid_until`
A contract attached to a context rule; the account calls its `enforce` after authenticating (hooks `install`, `uninstall`, `enforce`)
The expression the interpreter stores per (account, rule) and evaluates in `enforce`
No counterpart: Perch decides in the account
The smallest unit of XLM: {{fact:stroops-per-xlm}} stroops make one XLM
The proof assistant whose kernel checks the theorems
